description: Shokupan, the quintessential Japanese milk bread, is renowned for its incredibly soft, fluffy texture and subtle sweetness. This beloved loaf uses the tangzhong method to create a bread so tender it practically melts in your mouth. Perfect for sandwiches, toast, or simply enjoyed on its own, it is a truly delightful baking experience.

ingredients.notes: for main dough, plus more for dusting

instructions.title: Prepare the Tangzhong
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, whisk together 1/2 cup water and 2 tablespoons bread flour until smooth. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a paste-like consistency, about 2-3 minutes. It should form ripples when stirred. Remove from heat, transfer to a small bowl, cover with plastic wrap directly touching the surface to prevent a skin from forming, and let it cool completely to room temperature (about 30-60 minutes).

instructions.title: Mix the Dough Ingredients
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl (or stand mixer bowl), combine the remaining 3 cups bread flour, granulated sugar, salt, and instant dry yeast. Whisk well to combine. Add the cooled tangzhong, lukewarm whole milk, and lukewarm heavy cream to the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or the dough hook attachment on low speed until a shaggy dough forms. Cover the bowl and let it rest for 10 minutes to allow the flour to hydrate.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Add the softened unsalted butter to the dough. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface or with a stand mixer on medium-low speed for 10-15 minutes, or until it becomes smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test. The dough should be slightly tacky but not sticky. Form the dough into a smooth ball.

instructions.title: First Proof (Bulk Fermentation)
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place the dough ball in the bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until it has doubled in size. This is the first proof.

instructions.title: Shape the Loaf
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough to release the air. Transfer it to a lightly floured surface and divide it into 3 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a flat oval, then fold the top third down to the center and the bottom third up to the center. Turn the dough over and roll it into a tight cylinder. Place the three shaped dough cylinders seam-side down into a lightly greased 9x5 inch loaf pan, arranging them side-by-side.

instructions.title: Second Proof & Bake
instructions.text: Cover the loaf pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for another 45-60 minutes, or until the dough has risen about 1 inch above the rim of the pan. Preheat your oven to 350F (175C) during the last 15 minutes of proofing. Optionally, brush the top of the risen dough with a beaten egg for a golden crust. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 190-200F (88-93C).

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, immediately remove the loaf from the pan and transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing. This prevents the bottom from becoming soggy and ensures the best texture. Enjoy your homemade Shokupan slices plain, toasted, or as part of your favorite sandwich!

tips: For the softest Shokupan, ensure your tangzhong is fully cooled before adding it to the main dough. This prevents it from cooking the yeast.
Kneading until the dough passes the windowpane test is crucial for Shokupan's signature fluffy texture. It indicates proper gluten development.
Store leftover Shokupan in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 3 days, or freeze slices for longer storage. Reheat gently for best results.
